latest.content:
17 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0900V
CRISM Therapeutics Corporation
17 September 2026
17 September 2026
CRISM Therapeutics Corporation
(‘CRISM’, ‘CRISM Therapeutics’ or the ‘Company’)
Appointment of Non-executive Chair
CRISM Therapeutics Corporation (AIM: CRTX),
a UK clinical-stage drug delivery company focused on the localised and sustained delivery of chemotherapy drugs
,
is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr Charles Spicer as Non-Executive
Chair
with effect from 1 October 2026
.
Following Dr Spicer’s appointment
Andrew Webb will step down as Interim Executive
Chairman and resume his role as
the Company
’s Chief Executive Officer.
Charles brings over 25 years of senior executive, non-executive, and corporate finance experience within the medtech, life science, and healthcare investment sectors. His extensive track record in scaling AIM-quoted healthcare companies and executing healthcare capital markets and commercial transactions is directly relevant to CRISM as it advances its lead candidate, irinotecan-ChemoSeed®, in its registration-grade Phase 2 clinical trial in glioblastoma.
Charles currently also serves as Non-Executive
Chair of
EMV Capital plc (AIM: EMVC), a venture capital company specialising in deep tech and life sciences, as well as
Chair of
Aethox
Limited, a
Kings College London biopharmaceutical spin-out, and medtech innovator Cryogenx
Limited
.
Charles previously served for eight years as Non-Executive Chair of Creo Medical Group plc (AIM: CREO), overseeing its transformation from an early-stage UK company through to its IPO on AIM, scale-up, and global commercial expansion. He also served for fourteen years as a Panel Chair for the National Institute for Health and Care Research (‘NIHR’) Invention for Innovation (‘i4i’) product development awards. Prior to that, he served as Chief Executive of MDY Healthcare plc, a strategic med tech investor, following a distinguished corporate finance career as Head of Healthcare Corporate Finance at both Numis Securities and Nomura International.
Andrew Webb, Interim Executive Chairman of CRISM Therapeutics, commented:
"We are delighted to welcome Charles to the Board of CRISM as Non-Executive Chair. Charles joins us as patient recruitment is underway for our Phase 2 clinical trial in glioblastoma and our pipeline in prostate cancer is progressing well. His track record in guiding AIM-quoted healthcare companies through clinical scale-up, capital markets execution and commercial growth will be invaluable to CRISM. His deep expertise will position us well as we focus on improving the lives of patients and building long-term shareholder value."
Charles Spicer, incoming Non-Executive Chair of CRISM Therapeutics, commented:
"CRISM’s ChemoSeed technology represents a highly innovative approach to solving one of oncology’s most persistent challenges, delivering sustained, localised chemotherapy directly to solid tumours while limiting systemic toxicity. Having followed the Company’s progress, I am impressed by the strength of the pre-clinical and clinical data generated to date, the recent regulatory milestones achieved in both the UK and US, and the team’s disciplined execution. I look forward to working closely with the Board to support the Company as we advance through Phase 2 clinical evaluation and look to maximise the commercial potential of the ChemoSeed platform."
AIM Schedule Two (g) Disclosures
In accordance with Rule 17 and Schedule 2(g) of the AIM Rules for Companies, the following information is disclosed in relation to Dr Charles Alexander Evan Spicer, aged 61:
Current directorships
Directorships held in the past 5 years
EMV Capital plc
Korn Wall Limited
Aethox Therapeutics Ltd
Creo Medical Group plc
The Garden Museum
IXICO plc
Cryogenx Ltd
MJ Hudson Group plc
Dr Spicer was a director of MJ Hudson Group plc until December 2022, which was placed into Creditors’ Winding Up pursuant to Article 157A(a) of the Companies (Jersey) Law 1991 on 4 September 2023.
Dr Spicer does not hold any shares in the Company.
There are no further disclosures required to be made in respect of the appointment of Dr Charles Spicer under AIM Rule 17 and Schedule 2(g) of the AIM Rules for Companies.

About CRISM Therapeutics Corporation
CRISM Therapeutics Corporation
has developed an innovative drug delivery technology to improve the clinical performance of cancer treatments for solid tumours through the local delivery of chemotherapy drugs.
ChemoSeed, CRISM's lead product, can be implanted directly into the tumour or the resection margin following the removal of a tumour. This directs that therapeutic concentrations of chemotherapy drugs reach the deep-seated tumour tissue or cover the entire resection margin. In the case of treating glioblastoma, ChemoSeeds can be implanted during surgery thereby bypassing the blood brain barrier, which prevents other treatments from being able to reach the tumour and be effective.
CRISM has commenced recruitment at the Company’s first clinical site for its registration-grade Phase 2 clinical trial of irinotecan-ChemoSeed in patients with surgically resectable glioblastoma.

CRISM Therapeutics Corporation
("CRISM", "CRISM Therapeutics" or the "Company")
Clinical Trial Update
Clinical Trial Site Activation and Commencement of Patient Recruitment
CRISM Therapeutics Corporation (AIM: CRTX),
a UK clinical-stage drug delivery company focused on the localised and sustained delivery of chemotherapy drugs
, is pleased to announce that the first clinical site for its Phase II study of irinotecan ChemoSeed® for the treatment of glioblastoma has now been formally activated and patient recruitment has started.
Formal site activation represents a significant milestone for ChemoSeed®'s clinical development programme and enables the clinical team to begin identifying, screening and enrolling eligible patients into the study.
As the study officially transitions into its active clinical phase, the Company's immediate operational focus is the screening and clinical assessment of eligible participants. The next key milestone will be the successful treatment of the first patient with ChemoSeed®, and the Company will provide a further update once this has been achieved.
Professor Christopher McConville, Chief Scientific Officer of CRISM Therapeutics, commented:
"The activation of our first clinical site and opening of the study for patient recruitment is an important milestone for CRISM and the ChemoSeed® programme. We are delighted that the study has now entered active patient recruitment and that the clinical team can begin identifying and screening potential patients."
"We would like to thank the investigators, NHS Trust, clinical site team and our clinical partners for their work, and we look forward to updating shareholders as the study progresses."
Professor Garth Cruickshank, Emeritus Professor of Neurosurgery at the University of Birmingham and member of CRISM's Scientific Advisory Board, added:
"Opening this study to patient recruitment is a significant milestone in developing this novel treatment platform. Glioblastoma remains one of the most challenging cancers to treat, with recurrence frequently occurring close to the site of the original tumour despite surgery and subsequent treatment.
"ChemoSeed has been designed to address this challenge by delivering irinotecan directly into the tumour resection margin at the time of surgery, when the residual tumour burden is at its lowest. This approach has the potential to achieve, safe but sustained, high concentrations of chemotherapy at the site where it is most needed, while limiting systemic exposure with a drug proven to be active against glioblastoma.
"With the clinical site now activated and open to recruitment, we can begin the process of identifying suitable patients for the study and evaluating this approach in the clinical setting. I am very pleased to see the trial reach this stage."
-Ends-

company_30s.what_they_do: CRTX is a small‑cap biotechnology firm that is developing a new drug platform aimed at treating advanced prostate cancer. The company is in the early stages of clinical development, focusing on a novel therapeutic approach that could offer a higher response rate than current standard treatments.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers among men worldwide, with a huge unmet need for more effective therapies. CRTX’s platform could carve out a niche in a crowded market by offering a different mechanism of action. If successful, the company could capture a sizeable share of a multi‑billion‑pound market.
company_30s.current_state: CRTX is still in the pre‑revenue phase. It has just finished Phase 1 funding, received a government grant, and is actively recruiting patients for its next trial. The company is still burning cash, but the recent funding rounds and grant indicate that investors see potential in its pipeline.

rns_narrative: The company has been moving its governance forward by appointing a new non‑executive chair, signalling a desire to strengthen oversight. This coincides with the start of patient recruitment and a clinical trial update that highlights progress in early‑phase studies. In parallel, the firm has secured a government grant and issued options, both of which improve its financial footing.

These events can be grouped into three themes: 1) leadership and governance changes, 2) clinical development milestones, and 3) financial support and shareholder activity. Together they suggest the firm is actively working to stabilise operations and build credibility with regulators and investors.

The latest announcements indicate that the company is not just surviving but actively positioning itself for a potential breakthrough. The timing of the grant and option grant right before the trial update is a clear signal that the company is preparing for a future product launch.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the government grant, Phase 1 funding, and the new chair as evidence that the company is gaining institutional support. They believe the upcoming trial results could unlock a large upside.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the market has not yet accepted the RNS and that the company’s history of dilution could erode shareholder value. They fear a negative trial outcome or regulatory setbacks could leave the stock stranded.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has shifted from neutral to slightly bullish over the last few days as more people highlighted the grant and Phase 1 funding. The chatter is still low, but the tone is becoming more optimistic.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for CRTX is dead, meaning there is no current public interest. This is a perfect contrarian environment – a surprise catalyst could trigger a large move.

near_term_catalysts: Positive data from the ongoing Phase 1 trial – a clear signal of safety and preliminary efficacy.
A formal regulatory meeting or approval milestone, such as a meeting with the EMA or FDA to discuss next‑phase plans.
A licensing announcement or partnership with a larger pharma that would provide additional funding and credibility.
A spike in trading volume that breaks the tight compression seen in the APEX score, indicating fresh buying interest.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 10‑20% jump in volume after the trial update, a price break above the 20‑day moving average, or any announcement that the trial met its primary endpoints. These would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a recovery cycle – the price is still far below its recent peak and the APEX compression suggests a potential breakout. Confirmation will likely come within the next 2–3 months if the trial data is positive.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is in a deep crash, and if it delivers positive Phase 1 data it could rebound to roughly halfway between its all‑time low and high. That would be a 200–300% upside from the current level, while the risk is limited to the price we buy at. The signal hierarchy suggests that a deep crash (Green or Orange) is the best environment for a big bounce, and the recent funding events add conviction.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is a negative trial result or a regulatory setback that would keep the stock stuck at its current low. Even with the grant, the company still has no revenue and could face further dilution if more shares are issued. In that case the downside is limited to the current price but the upside potential evaporates.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: current price (e.g., 0.00p). Potential gain: up to 2–3× that if the stock recovers to 50–70% of its peak. The asymmetry is highly favorable – a small loss for a large upside.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear volume spike following a positive trial announcement. Size the position so that a 5‑10% drop would not wipe out the trade. Place a stop just below the recent support level. Target 50% of the all‑time high as the primary profit target, with a secondary target at 70% of the high.

playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate terminal risks such as bankruptcy or delisting at this time.
